title: Rename an Android package
tagline: Move the code, change the namespace, and rebuild before you trust a release.
intro: A package name is written in three places: the folder path, the package line in every file, and the namespace in Gradle. A rename has to move all three together.

sections.title: Overview
sections.summary: Let the IDE move the files; do the Gradle part by hand.

blocks.caption: From com.old.app to com.new.app without a broken release.

items.label: Expand the packages
items.detail: Untick Compact Middle Packages so each part of the name is its own folder
explain: With compaction on, com.old.app shows as one row, and a rename can only change the whole thing or nothing.
It is in the Project panel's gear menu → Tree Appearance. Only the view changes; nothing on disk moves.

items.label: Refactor → Rename
items.detail: Renaming the folder through Refactor rewrites every package and import line too
explain: Right-click the segment to change → Refactor → Rename → Rename package. Renaming in Finder would move the files and break every import.
Rename one segment at a time: com.old.app becomes com.new.app by renaming old to new.

items.label: Check the debug source set
items.detail: Files outside main, such as ReactNativeFlipper in debug, can keep the old import
explain: The refactor covers the source set you are in. src/debug/java/… is a separate tree that React Native templates put Flipper setup in.
A debug build that fails with 'cannot find symbol' right after a rename is almost always this file.

items.label: Namespace in Gradle
items.detail: The namespace in app/build.gradle names the generated R and BuildConfig classes
explain: Change namespace "com.old.app" to the new name, then Sync. Until then, R still lives in the old package and every screen fails to compile.
applicationId is separate: it is the id on the Play Store. Change it only if this is meant to be a different app.

items.label: Clean and rebuild
items.detail: Clean, rebuild, run, then build the release .apk and .aab to be sure
explain: Stale intermediates still reference the old package, and the release task is sometimes the only one that trips over them.
A debug run that works proves little here; the release build is the check that the rename is finished.

items: Open the android folder in Android Studio.
Project panel gear → Tree Appearance → untick Compact Middle Packages.
Right-click the package segment → Refactor → Rename.
Open src/debug and fix any file still importing the old package, e.g. ReactNativeFlipper.
Change namespace in app/build.gradle and click Sync.
Build → Clean Project, Rebuild Project, run, then build the release .apk and .aab.

blocks.caption: app/build.gradle — applicationId only if the store id should change too

body: Changing applicationId on a published app creates a new listing; existing users will not get it as an update.
